sections.text:
The exploration menu is LOCKED as eight repeatable assessments:

1. **The Unknown** — candidate investigates a fixed fictional systems-failure file, with limited scripted questions, then briefs what happened, what is known/unknown, and next actions.
2. **The Build** — candidate constructs a physical structure from a fixed materials kit across a defined span; payload changes mid-exercise; test and debrief follow.
3. **The Teach** — candidate teaches a non-job topic they genuinely know/care about with one object/page and no slides; assessors ask fixed questions and deliberately misunderstand one point for repair.
4. **The Hand-Off** — candidate inherits a fixed project file, interviews a scripted prior owner holding undisclosed facts, then briefs an executive sponsor on what was inherited and what happens next.
5. **Judgment Under Trade-Offs** — candidate chooses among three viable options in a fixed operating scenario with explicit costs/probabilities; receives a new fact and may retain or change the decision.
6. **Critique** — candidate evaluates a polished but intentionally mixed-quality recommendation, meets the scripted author, and recommends proceed/modify/stop with concrete next action.
7. **Prioritization** — candidate receives a fixed Monday-morning board of competing issues, sorts do-now/delegate/schedule/not-today, then reprioritizes after a standardized curveball.
8. **Self-Correction** — candidate makes a decision on a fixed market-entry case, receives material new evidence, then issues a second decision and explains what changed and why.

Packets, timings, prompts, and assessor scripts are standardized. The chosen assessment is explained to the candidate as the question Sable Harbor is trying to answer, not hidden as personality theater.

sections.heading: Offers and compensation
Ownership
sections.text: Sable Harbor should operate in the spirit of broad employee ownership without becoming a legal co-op. The target architecture is fair cash compensation + meaningful profit participation + long-duration employee ownership. A conservatively structured ESOP or similar trust is preferred over a debt-heavy ownership transaction. Ownership should compound with continuity while corporate governance remains with the Board and management.

sections.heading: Career architecture and mobility
sections.text:
No up-or-out. Employees may deepen professionally, manage, teach, rotate, or move across businesses/geographies. Professional/technical excellence is a first-class destination.

Internal mobility is a right to explore, not a privilege granted by the current manager. Current managers may consult but may not silently hoard talent. Manager effectiveness includes development and healthy talent flow across Sable Harbor.

A separate **Next Chapter** conversation asks what interests the employee, what they want to learn/build, and what small bet/rotation/assignment might make that real. It is not compensation theater and is distinct from ordinary work feedback.

Performance discussion is deliberately lightweight and candid, centered on two questions: **How is the work going?** and **Where could you go from here?** No surprise annual files and no spreadsheet-ranking culture.

Each employee must have a route outside the line manager through a P&C talent partner when manager/employee fit is poor. High-performing team chemistry may be preserved deliberately, but teams must remain permeable; chemistry does not create clique immunity or fiefdom rights.

sections.heading: Management formation
sections.text:
Management is a profession. Prospective managers receive formation in law, compensation, mobility, hiring, talent management, judgment, and difficult human situations. Practical simulations matter more than slideware. Management appointment is reversible without stigma; returning to a professional track is not failure.

Talent/scout education occurs at multiple leadership levels. Strong prospective scouts may complete a deeper scout qualification and rotational tour before or after first management appointment.

sections.heading: Learning
sections.text: P&C owns access, opportunity, mobility, and career architecture. J2 Education owns education as a profession. Businesses own learning through real work. Learning time is work and is not expected to be made up privately.

sections.heading: Workforce planning, redeployment, and reductions
sections.text:
Hiring is a long-duration capital decision. Overhiring is treated as a management risk.

Before a reduction, Sable Harbor conducts a continuity review across the enterprise: what work is disappearing, what capability exists, where else it might be productive, what can be retrained/redeployed, and whether external hiring should pause for equivalent needs. A standing continuity reserve may fund bridging, relocation, and retraining so local managers are not punished for preserving enterprise capability.

**Automation creates capacity, not casualties.** Sable Harbor does not eliminate productive people solely to polish a margin or because automation made a task cheaper. Productivity gains first trigger the question: what more can this capability do?

If reduction becomes genuinely unavoidable, leadership exhausts reasonable reversible levers first, explains the facts and sequence candidly, and accepts visible leadership sacrifice before asking employees to bear the irreversible action. Selection follows work and capability rather than convenience. Separations are handled with dignity, meaningful severance/benefit treatment, real placement assistance, and truthful communication.

A RIF is treated as management necessity/failure, not employee moral failure.

sections.heading: Succession
sections.text: Succession preserves capital. Critical roles should not be single-human dependencies. Succession is role resilience and capability development, not a secret aristocracy or declared crown-prince program. The enterprise asks who can cover a role temporarily, who could hold it now, and who could grow into it later; development follows from that analysis.

sections.heading: Employee listening
sections.text: No employee panopticon. Listening relies on voluntary human channels, small groups, stay/exit conversations, manager presence, P&C relationships, and material issue escalation. Passive behavior surveillance is rejected as a substitute for trust.

sections.heading: 7. Technology Services doctrine
sections.text:
Enterprise IT is an internal product and engineering organization. Its customer is the employee/business capability that must work. The success criterion is not ticket closure; it is restored and improved capability.

Business/product engineering remains inside the businesses. Technology Services builds the paved road beneath it.

sections.heading: Core technology product lines
Operating doctrine
Security
Resilience
sections.text: Resilience is an operating capability, not a binder. Begin with what must continue, set meaningful recovery/recovery-point objectives, test restoration in reality, include critical third parties, remove single-human key dependencies, establish temporary crisis authority, and learn from incidents/near misses.

sections.heading: AI and data
sections.text:
Sable Harbor AI should be a secure capability fabric rather than a policy war over model brands. Use tiered capability: local/private models where bounded privacy/predictability matter, Sable Harbor-hosted models as capability grows, and frontier models where their added capability is justified.

Central technology builds secure routing, sandboxing, identity, logging, and infrastructure. Businesses experiment and build inside those guardrails. Govern data, authority, consequence, and capability — not the marketing label “AI.”

Every human, service, device, and consequential AI agent has an identity. Agents receive explicit scoped delegation and do not silently inherit the full authority of a human. Delegation narrows rather than expands. Break-glass access is time-bounded and reviewed. Access reviews should become anomaly-driven where possible rather than spreadsheet rituals.

Detailed control/evidence mechanics belong in the Common Controls Framework and NAILEX/assessment work, not in this constitutional doctrine.

sections.heading: 8. Decision and autonomy doctrine
sections.text:
Sable Harbor assigns consequential decisions to one accountable owner. Consultation may be broad; accountability is singular. No one owns a decision merely by being in the room.

Default to judgment. Train for it. Evaluate decision quality against what was reasonably knowable at the time, not merely the eventual outcome. Outcome quality and decision quality are not the same thing.

Documentation is triggered by stakes, not habit. Routine low-consequence decisions do not require a ritual record. Consequential decisions should be legible enough to preserve owner, material evidence, serious alternatives, dissent, reasoning, and a revisit trigger. Existential/reserved decisions receive the higher governance treatment already established elsewhere.

**Autonomy does not require justification; restrictions on autonomy do.**

Meetings are expensive. Default to no meeting. A meeting should have an identifiable purpose, owner, and reason the attendees need synchronous interaction. Decision notes, direct calls, or asynchronous work are preferred when they achieve the result at lower cognitive/coordination cost.

sections.heading: 9. Capital allocation rhythm
10. Planning and performance rhythm
Ring 1 — Authority Core
sections.text: A very small group able to assemble quickly when enterprise authority must act. Its existence is about speed and decision rights, not representation. Single accountable decision ownership still applies.

sections.heading: Ring 2 — Enterprise Staff / information network
sections.text: A broad NVIDIA-like ring, roughly 20–40 people depending on actual information value: business presidents and key functional/institutional leaders. Membership follows relevance and information value rather than entitlement to a cabinet seat. The purpose is information symmetry, direct challenge, enterprise context, and reduced loss-through-hierarchy.

sections.heading: Ring 3 — Issue Rooms
sections.text:
Temporary Toyota-like problem rooms form around consequential issues with one owner and all material knowledge/expertise brought directly into the room. They dissolve when the problem resolves.

The person closest to the problem has unfiltered voice even when they do not own the decision. **Hierarchy sets accountability, not epistemology.**

J2 supports information coherence and shared factual/uncertainty context across these rings but does not own executive decisions.

sections.heading: 12. Information architecture
sections.text:
Default open inside Sable Harbor where responsible disclosure allows. Restriction follows information nature and actual obligation, not rank.

J2 synthesizes: what is known, what changed, what is assumed, where confidence/dissent/gaps sit. It does not command the enterprise.

The authority core receives decision-ready context; enterprise staff receives broad context; issue rooms receive depth. Relevant expertise may be pulled directly across hierarchy. Material information may reach J2 outside the management chain when a person reasonably believes ordinary hierarchy is filtering/distorting it.

sections.heading: 13. Federated professional practices
sections.text:
**Functions own the profession; businesses own the work.**

Corporate functions/practice leaders may own standards, profession development, qualifications, talent cultivation, assurance/challenge, and shared methods. They do not gain default day-to-day operating authority over business functional teams.

A business CFO, P&C lead, technologist, or other professional belongs simultaneously to the business, their profession, and Sable Harbor. There is no dual-decision matrix. When conflict arises, identify the type of decision:

- operating decision → business authority;
- professional/enterprise standard → functional standard authority;
- reserved enterprise matter → escalate to the defined enterprise owner/body.

Practice leaders are conveners/stewards, not shadow executives.

sections.heading: 14. Portfolio architecture
sections.text:
A named product/project does not become a business automatically. A Sable Harbor business earns that status through coherent market/economic logic, genuine leadership capacity, and enough permanence that autonomy improves decisions.

Default structure: **Sable Harbor → business → operating unit.** No new operating-group layer until demonstrated need exists.

Business presidents run their businesses end-to-end inside enterprise boundaries. Corporate exists to make businesses stronger, not to recreate their functions at headquarters.

Capital is the primary connective tissue. People, methods, technology, education, and professional knowledge can move across businesses without creating a command matrix.

Acquisitions may be integrated into an existing business, operated as a business, or incubated for learning with explicit intent. Long-duration ownership is preferred, but long duration is not eternity.

sections.heading: 15. Physical headquarters doctrine
sections.text:
Headquarters is in **Sacramento, California**. It is a formidable, beautiful long-duration institutional campus, not a gaudy tower or performatively austere office. It should feel like an advanced research/industrial institution: excellent materials, strong geometry, warm human interiors, serious common/project/education space, and landscaping that rewards presence.

The canonical September 3 exterior reference depicts contemporary glass, metal, concrete, and warm wood; landscaped grasses, stone, trees, water, and a clear illuminated SABLE HARBOR / HEADQUARTERS / SACRAMENTO, CALIFORNIA monument. No invented Capitol or San Jose setting is canon. Canonical source-image SHA-256 at approval: `2bf5a1209b9c3ece435271f2fbf5a3c827bbbccf242ea4ee60535749ccee9d92`.

Corporate leaders are expected to spend meaningful time in the businesses. Headquarters is a working institutional center, not the place where all important people permanently retreat.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Management presented a proposed growth financing led by Harrison Vale Partners. The Board considered whether the financing supported Sable Harbor's post-Crossing productization, repeatability, reliability, and commercial scale without converting the company into an investor-controlled operating model.

sections.heading: Materials reviewed
sections.text: The Board reviewed management's financing memorandum, proposed use of proceeds, capitalization and dilution analysis, investor-rights summary, operating plan, productization roadmap, implementation-capacity constraints, reliability/security investment needs, and commercial pipeline analysis.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text:
The Board discussed the risk that services-era success could be mistaken for product repeatability. Directors emphasized that institutional capital should follow the Crossing-era product breakthrough rather than rewrite it as investor rescue. Harry van der Velde challenged the downside financing case and the company's ability to preserve operating independence if customer growth outpaced deployment discipline. Dr. Galiullina questioned whether technical and reliability investment was sufficient before broader commercial acceleration.

The Board determined that Harrison Vale's vertical enterprise-software and industrial-data experience was strategically useful if accompanied by balanced governance, no ordinary-course veto, no privileged commercial channel, and clear distinction between investor advice and company authority.

sections.heading: Resolutions
sections.text:
After discussion, the Board approved management's entry into definitive documents for an approximately **$48 million** growth financing led by **Harrison Vale Partners**, subject to final legal review and no material adverse change in negotiated terms.

The Board approved the principal use of proceeds for repeatable deployment, productization, reliability and security maturity, commercial growth, customer operations, and finance/people systems needed to support scale.

The Board approved one Harrison Vale board seat while the negotiated ownership threshold remained satisfied. The Board appointed **Evan Mercer** as Harrison Vale's initial board representative effective upon closing.

The Board reaffirmed that investor directors serve as directors of Sable Harbor and not as constituency representatives with ordinary-course veto rights.

The Board approves the reserved-matters, subsidiary-autonomy, rapid-adjudication, Assumption of Risk, abstention, decision-quality, AAR, conflict-integrity, and founder-authority doctrines as controlled governance records.

The Board ratifies **J2 — Judgment & Junction** as an internal Sable Harbor institutional capability, not a legal entity or customer-facing business line, consisting of a small Headquarters, Contact, Judgment, Orientation, Junction Advisory Group, and Education.

The Board ratifies the J2 identity package and letterhead system as controlled internal identity collateral subordinate to the Sable Harbor corporate document standard.

The Board approves **Alexandria** as the umbrella institutional intelligence environment and ratifies the naming and purpose of **Pinakes** as the human catalog/portal, **Semaphore** as the cable-like traffic system, **Canon** as the institutional knowledge corpus, and **Daedalus** as the personal non-authoritative AI research companion.

The Board approves the Daedalus AI-authority boundary: intellectual aggression without institutional authority; no authoritative record write; no self-promotion into Canon/Judgment/Semaphore/EIB; no institutional authority except by quoting human-authored records; personal instance isolation; content-free skill sharing; and universal read with bounded disclosure as an architectural direction subject to future runtime controls.

The Board approves the corporate document system requiring canonical Markdown, controlled corporate publication where appropriate, and structured representation where appropriate, with source/publication/catalog reconciliation.

The Board directs Corporate Governance, J2 Headquarters, Orientation, and the relevant owning functions to maintain the controlled-document index, structured registers, validation routines, and supersession boundaries so that polished publications do not create canon beyond the source records they publish.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: People & Culture exists to make Sable Harbor an exceptional place for exceptional people to do serious work over a long career. **Continuity is capital.** Experience, judgment, relationships, craft, and institutional memory should compound rather than be treated as interchangeable labor.

sections.heading: Service doctrine
sections.text:
The necessary HR plumbing—payroll, benefits, leave/accommodations, required-training administration, employee relations/investigations, separations, and records—should be nearly invisible when healthy. One human front door is preferred. Self-service removes friction; it never becomes a shield that prevents human help. Recurring pain is a defect. Default to fewer processes and fewer mandatory steps.

P&C owns the employee experience of mandatory learning; the function creating the legal/security/safety/other requirement owns the substantive reason and content authority.

**Never give with one hand and take with the other.** Benefits and programs are tested for friction in money, time, hassle, and stigma from the lived perspective of the least senior employee affected.

sections.heading: Work and workplace
sections.text: **Work where the work works best.** Hybrid work is genuine where the role permits it. There is no arbitrary office quota substituting for judgment. Employees are expected to recognize when presence materially improves collaboration, mentoring, coordination, or human interaction. The office must earn the commute. Free on-premise parking is part of the Sacramento workplace principle where driving is a normal commute mode; useful transit support is encouraged as well.

sections.heading: Talent philosophy
sections.text:
Sable Harbor seeks proven masters, high-slope early-career talent, unconventional excellence conventional screens miss, and people who know something Sable Harbor does not.

Talent cycle: **Spot → Assess → Evaluate → Recruit → Develop → Run.** Talent scouting is a prestigious rotational capability for sufficiently mature practitioners, including people outside P&C. The side door creates visibility, not a lower hiring bar.

Once Sable Harbor asks a candidate for meaningful human time, Sable Harbor owes a human conclusion. Substantive candidates receive real, respectful feedback if not selected.

sections.heading: Selection flow
Exploration assessment library
sections.text:
- **The Unknown** — fixed fictional systems-failure investigation with limited scripted questions and final known/unknown/next-action briefing.
- **The Build** — fixed physical-materials construction problem with a mid-exercise payload change, test, and debrief.
- **The Teach** — candidate teaches a non-job subject they genuinely know, no slides, followed by fixed questions and a deliberate misunderstanding to repair.
- **The Hand-Off** — candidate inherits a fixed project, interviews a scripted former owner holding undisclosed facts, then briefs the sponsor.
- **Judgment Under Trade-Offs** — fixed operating choice among three viable options, followed by new evidence and a second decision.
- **Critique** — fixed polished recommendation containing genuine strengths and flaws; candidate challenges the scripted author and recommends proceed/modify/stop.
- **Prioritization** — fixed Monday-morning issue board sorted into do-now/delegate/schedule/not-today, then reprioritized after a curveball.
- **Self-Correction** — fixed case decision, new evidence, revised decision, and explanation of what changed.

Packets, timing, prompts, and assessor scripts are standardized.

sections.heading: Offers, compensation, and ownership
sections.text:
Sable Harbor offers what it believes is fair if the candidate accepts immediately. Negotiation skill does not determine compensation; new information may correct a bad initial offer. Salary-history games are rejected.

There is **no up-or-out system**. Professional and technical tracks may out-earn management. Management is a separate profession, not the required destination for status or pay. Counteroffers should be rare because compensation health is reviewed before resignation forces the issue.

Long-duration value creation should produce long-duration employee economic participation. Direction: strong cash pay, meaningful profit participation, and broad employee ownership through a conservatively structured ESOP or similar trust rather than a debt-heavy ownership transaction. Employee ownership does not displace Board governance or management authority.

sections.heading: Careers and mobility
sections.text:
Internal mobility is a right to explore. Current managers may consult but may not silently veto or hoard talent. Employees may deepen professionally, manage, teach, rotate, change business lines, or change geography.

Ordinary work feedback stays lightweight and candid: **How is the work going?** and **Where could you go from here?** A separate Next Chapter conversation explores curiosity, latent strengths, new builds, rotations, and small experiments. No surprise annual files and no stack-ranking spreadsheet culture.

Each employee has access to a P&C talent partner outside the line manager for fit/mobility problems. High-performing team chemistry may be preserved, but teams remain permeable and chemistry creates no clique immunity.

sections.heading: Management formation
sections.text:
Management is a profession. Prospective managers receive real formation in law, compensation, mobility, hiring, the talent cycle, judgment, and difficult human situations, with practical simulations rather than slideware. Management appointment is reversible without stigma; returning to a professional track is not failure.

Talent/scout education occurs at multiple leadership levels. Strong candidates may enter deeper scout qualification and a roughly 12-month rotational scouting tour.

sections.heading: Learning
sections.text: P&C owns opportunity, access, mobility, and career architecture. J2 Education owns education as a professional discipline. Businesses own learning through actual work. Learning time is work.

sections.heading: Workforce continuity
sections.text:
Hiring is a long-duration capital decision. Overhiring is a management risk.

Before any reduction, Sable Harbor conducts a continuity review across the enterprise: disappearing work, transferable capability, retraining, redeployment, relocation, and whether external hiring should pause. A continuity reserve may fund productive bridging so local budgets do not punish enterprise retention.

**Automation creates capacity, not casualties.** Sable Harbor does not eliminate productive people merely to polish a margin or because automation made current tasks cheaper. Productivity first raises the question: what more can these people do?

If reduction is genuinely unavoidable, reasonable reversible levers, redeployment, retraining, and visible leadership sacrifice precede the irreversible action. Selection follows work/capability, not convenience. Communication is candid. Severance/benefits and placement support are meaningful and dignified. A RIF is a management necessity/failure, not an employee moral failure.

sections.heading: Succession and listening
sections.text:
Succession is capital preservation. Critical roles should not depend on one human. The purpose is role resilience and capability development, not a secret chosen-one list.

P&C rejects the employee panopticon. Listening relies on voluntary human channels, small groups, stay/exit conversations, manager presence, P&C relationships, and material escalation—not passive behavioral surveillance.

sections.heading: Anti-bureaucracy rule
sections.text: P&C has a standing duty to challenge bureaucracy, including its own. Care may not become paternalism. A process that cannot explain the work, legal, safety, continuity, or human problem it solves carries the burden of proof.

sections.text:
The default instrument is a **contractual phantom carry plan** tied to the economic performance of Sable Harbor Advisory. It does not itself issue voting equity, board rights, management authority, information rights beyond those required to administer the plan, or ownership of Sable Harbor intellectual property.

If Advisory is later placed in a separate legal entity, the plan may be converted, exchanged, or replaced with an economically equivalent instrument subject to approved legal and tax treatment.

sections.heading: 3. Carry pool
sections.text: The Advisory Carry Pool equals **20% of Excess Advisory Economic Profit** after the annual hurdle and required reserves.

sections.heading: 3.1 Economic profit
sections.text:
For carry purposes:

`Advisory Economic Profit = recognized Advisory operating profit + approved Atlas-related Advisory contribution - direct matter losses - approved shared-service allocations - risk/claims charges - required investment reserves`

The calculation excludes accounting maneuvers whose principal purpose is to increase or suppress carry. Finance owns the calculation methodology and consistency.

sections.heading: 3.2 Hurdle
sections.text:
Carry participates only after Advisory has earned:

1. a full return of current-period operating losses carried forward;
2. required professional-liability, warranty, transfer-support and working-capital reserves; and
3. an annual hurdle equal to the greater of:
   - **10% of allocated Advisory operating capital**, or
   - the enterprise-approved cost-of-capital charge for Advisory.

There is no carry on gross revenue, backlog, bookings, or uncollected outcome fees.

sections.heading: 4. Units
sections.text:
The carry pool is represented by **10,000 notional Carry Units**.

Units are an allocation mechanism only. They are not shares.

The annual distributable carry attributable to a participant is:

`Distributable Carry × participant vested units / total vested participating units`

Unallocated units remain in the pool and do not accrue to any person.

sections.heading: 5. Eligibility
sections.text: Eligibility is restricted to former J2 professionals who complete an approved service gate.

sections.heading: Orientation
sections.text: Full commissioned Orientation tour plus one qualifying fellowship.

sections.heading: Judgment
sections.text: At least five years in a Judgment Officer position plus at least two years of substantive service in an actual Sable Harbor operating business line. JAG does not substitute for the operating-line requirement.

sections.heading: Contact
sections.text: At least four years in substantive Contact leadership with genuine responsibility for people and collection outcomes.

sections.heading: Education
sections.text: At least five years in J2 Education, including at least two years with substantive ownership of curriculum, professional formation, doctrine, fellowship, or evaluation programs used across J2. Pure administrative assignment does not qualify.

sections.heading: J2 Headquarters
sections.text: J2 Headquarters service does not independently create carry eligibility. A former J2 HQ professional qualifies only through a substantive underlying Contact, Judgment, Orientation, or Education gate. This avoids creating a route in which administrative proximity to J2 substitutes for professional intelligence service.

sections.heading: 6. No pre-service promise
sections.text:
No serving J2 person may receive, negotiate, reserve, model, preview, pre-clear, or be informally promised a carry grant.

No Advisory leader may tell a serving J2 person what grant they are likely to receive after service. Neutral public plan information may exist, but no individualized discussion may begin until J2 service is complete and the former professional initiates contact.

sections.heading: 7. Grant sizing
sections.text:
Carry eligibility permits consideration; it does not determine grant size.

Indicative grant ranges at appointment:

| Advisory professional level | Typical initial range |
|---|---:|
| Distinguished Principal | 300–900 units |
| Senior Principal | 175–500 units |
| Principal | 75–250 units |
| Senior Professional | 25–100 units |
| Other exceptional eligible professional | 10–75 units |

Ranges are guidelines, not entitlements. Grant sizing considers professional contribution, expected duration, scarcity, matter responsibility, method development, client impact, and institutional stewardship.

No grant may be sized based on privileged J2 information, access, relationships, or willingness to commercialize protected J2 knowledge.

sections.heading: 8. Vesting
sections.text:
Default vesting is **five years, 20% per completed year**, with no cliff.

Vesting is service-based and may be suspended during unpaid leave where legally permissible. The annual Carry Allocation Review may grant limited service credit for approved enterprise assignments, disability, military leave, or other protected circumstances.

Accelerated vesting is not used as an ordinary retention device.

sections.heading: 9. Distributions
10. Good leaver
11. Bad leaver
12. Clawback and malus
13. No matter-level carry
sections.text: Carry participates in durable Advisory economics, not individual matter fees. Matter-specific bonuses may exist, but a professional does not receive a fixed percentage of the outcome fee on a matter they personally control. This reduces incentive to distort baselines, scope, findings, or client acceptance.

sections.heading: 14. Dilution and new grants
sections.text:
New grants dilute existing unit percentages because the pool is shared. No participant has anti-dilution rights unless separately approved in a transaction.

The plan may reserve units for future generations of qualifying professionals. Carry is intended to remain a living professional institution rather than a permanently captured founder pool.

sections.heading: 15. Governance rights
16. Valuation and transaction treatment
sections.text: If a sale, spinout, merger, recapitalization, or separate capitalization of Advisory occurs, Finance and Legal determine an economically fair conversion of vested Carry Units. The guiding principle is to preserve the value of earned participation without converting the plan into a hidden governance instrument.

18. Cultural test
sections.text: The plan is functioning correctly only if a serving J2 professional can ignore it while serving, a former J2 professional can later build exceptional wealth through Advisory, and an outside or operating-line professional can still have an elite Advisory career without carry.

sections.heading: 1. Talent thesis
2.1 External market
sections.text:
Advisory may recruit aggressively from the external market. It may approach people directly, recruit by name, use scouts, hire unconventional profiles and pay a premium for unusual professional depth.

External hires may receive strong salary, bonus, profit participation, retention awards and other approved compensation. Advisory carry, however, is reserved to qualifying former J2 professionals.

sections.heading: 2.2 Sable Harbor operating business lines
sections.text:
Advisory may actively recruit from Sable Harbor operating lines, including by name.

The business reason is explicit: people who have actually operated mines, logistics networks, recovery systems, industrial programs, software deployments and other consequential systems carry tacit knowledge that is unusually valuable in client work.

Internal recruiting remains subject to enterprise mobility and continuity doctrine. Advisory may recruit; it may not sabotage an operating line's continuity or bypass ordinary transition obligations.

sections.heading: 2.3 Serving J2 personnel
3. Employee-initiated post-J2 entry
sections.text:
A former J2 professional may approach Advisory immediately after qualifying service is complete. There is no arbitrary cooling-off period.

The process must begin on the former J2 professional's initiative. Advisory may publish neutral information about career paths and eligibility rules, but it may not privately cultivate a serving individual.

No J2 manager, Orientation Officer, Judgment Officer, Contact leader, JAG participant or Education professional should need to wonder whether a judgment made in service will affect a promised Advisory role.

sections.heading: 4.1 Definition
sections.text:
Sable Harbor uses the term **carry** deliberately.

Advisory carry is long-duration economic participation in the value of the Advisory business. It is conceptually analogous to carried interest in investment businesses: the participant shares in durable value creation beyond salary and annual bonus.

It is not ordinary salary, a guaranteed deferred bonus, an automatic profit share for every employee, or a reward for leaving J2.

sections.heading: 4.2 Eligibility versus allocation
sections.text:
These are separate decisions.

**Eligibility** means a former J2 professional has completed the institutional-service gate required to be considered for carry.

**Allocation** means Advisory actually grants that person a defined economic interest under the carry plan.

A qualifying former J2 professional is not owed a carry percentage merely because eligibility exists.

sections.heading: 4.3 Why carry is J2-restricted
5.1 Orientation
sections.text:
A former commissioned Orientation Officer is carry-eligible after:

1. completing one full Orientation tour/commission; and
2. completing one qualifying fellowship.

This is the lowest additional Advisory gate because admission, formation and commission into Orientation already carry an unusually high institutional threshold.

Carry eligibility does not relax the permanent Orientation line-authority restriction.

sections.heading: 5.2 Judgment
sections.text:
A former Judgment Officer is carry-eligible after:

1. at least five years in a Judgment Officer position; and
2. at least two years of substantive service in an actual Sable Harbor operating business line.

The operating service may occur before or after Judgment service unless later doctrine specifies sequencing.

JAG does not count as the operating-line requirement. JAG is a temporary field-tour institution, not an operating line and not a permanent Judgment role.

sections.heading: 5.3 Contact
sections.text:
A former Contact professional is carry-eligible after at least four years in substantive Contact leadership.

Qualifying leadership requires genuine responsibility for people and collection outcomes. A title without corresponding accountability does not qualify.

Contact intentionally carries the highest threshold among the currently decided gates because it is a standing intelligence profession with less natural operating-line laterality and because leadership mastery is the clearest evidence that the candidate has progressed beyond technical collection skill alone.

sections.heading: 5.4 Education and J2 Headquarters

SMART's official description includes locomotive engineers, conductors and shortline operating employees, so the case need not assign engineers to another union by assumption. The property agreement summaries use eight-hour basic days, paid overtime, seniority and qualification rosters, representation during investigations, grievance steps, benefits and amendable dates. These are fictional negotiated terms, not copied national Class I terms. Hours-of-service, qualifications, drug/alcohol rules and operating protections apply independently of the commercial service promise or a CBA pay rule.

Fred Tolman's nine-month consulting role provides knowledge transfer; it does not preserve operating authority or create an exception to the retained management chain. Nora Ashcombe holds ARU day-one operating authority. Seth Kettering directs BS&T, Anika Soren directs dispatch, Paulina Dace directs mechanical work and Silas Wren coordinates railway safety. The corporate/finance corpus owns detailed biographies, compensation and the authoritative employee IDs.

The 14-event modern safety register spans 2014 through August 2026. It includes yard derailments, employee injuries, grade-crossing collisions, rule errors, contained fluid releases and the open contractor injury claim. Corrective actions connect to drainage, track, lifting equipment, training and the capital plan. Events are deliberately not uniformly clean. No shutdown order, concealed catastrophic defect or fictional government enforcement document is introduced.

The April 23, 2024 contractor pipe-loading injury carries a **$600,000 closing claim reserve**. A further **$700,000 possible adverse development** creates a $1.3 million adverse case. The potential seller indemnity above the closing reserve is not automatic cash or guaranteed collectibility. The **$1.75 million environmental reserve is separate**. Accident damage figures across years are not an additional 2025 expense schedule, and this internal register does not assert that every event was federally reportable or that a particular report was filed. Applicable-year definitions and thresholds must determine that question.

The August 14, 2026 receipt incident concerns sulfuric acid: a handheld outage delayed timestamp synchronization, while signed receipts, weights and material identity remained reconstructable. Corrective action adds an offline signed queue and dispatch reconciliation. It occurs after July 7 ordinary inbound commissioning and is not evidence of direct uranium custody.

The historical spine preserves the coal parent, Thomas R. Bell, the 1898 predecessor, approximate 1909 labor organization, 1953 failure and Walt Mercer's 1954 rescue. The remembered 1907 runaway and 1916 Bloodstone No. 2 mine disaster are retained with source uncertainty. Exact casualties are not promoted from a disputed appendix into recovered canon. Current SMART-TD terminology is not projected backward onto a 1909 coal workforce.

Direct product custody remains gated. Wyoming's uranium-recovery agreement covers specified milling/source-material activities; it does not make every nuclear activity a state license. The Part 40 carrier exemption has defined scope and exceptions and does not remove DOT hazardous-material obligations. Ordinary acid transloading requires assigned trained personnel, protection against car movement, written procedures, monitoring and closure checks. sections.heading: WIL-002 — Gid Voss's first instrumentation incident
sections.text:
**State:** LOCKED

Gid Voss's defining pre-Klein Sable Harbor incident occurs in **2018 at a coal preparation plant**. A mass-balance problem appears to show coal disappearing between mine feed, preparation, reject streams, and loadout. The initial working assumption is an integration or reconciliation defect.

Gid refuses to stop at the database boundary. The investigation establishes that the records are internally coherent but the physical assumptions behind them are not. Moisture and density assumptions are being applied inconsistently across measurement points, and a process stream treated administratively as ordinary reject is carrying recoverable coal. The apparent missing tonnage is therefore not theft, fraud, or a software arithmetic error. The represented process does not match the physical process closely enough to support the conclusion being drawn from it.

The incident establishes Gid's early reputation: when an integrated representation produces an impossible physical answer, test the world before patching the representation. It also gives the later eastern coal mandate a direct technical lineage rather than making coal an arbitrary regional expansion.

sections.heading: Gid Voss — pre-Sable Harbor background and personal texture
sections.text:
**State:** LOCKED narrative texture

Before Sable Harbor, Gid works as an unusually broad civilian industrial-systems specialist. Some assignments place him alongside government or government-adjacent technical teams examining industrial systems whose paperwork, instrumentation, physical configuration, or externally visible behavior do not reconcile cleanly. He is not an intelligence officer and the canon does not convert him into one. The experience does, however, make him comfortable with incomplete records, strange physical systems, and the possibility that a technically correct representation can still describe the wrong world.

Outside work, Gid restores and collects mechanical and industrial instruments, including **Curta calculators**. He also operates a small hot-air-balloon experience business on the side. It is a modest operation rather than a major commercial enterprise: a small number of balloons, sunrise flights, and a small crew. The business begins partly as a way to subsidize his own flying and persists because he genuinely likes flying, weather, and the quiet observational quality of ballooning.

sections.heading: Eli Hoberg
sections.text:
**State:** LOCKED; supersedes the OPEN surname placeholder

The Klein RF/communications engineer is **Ellis “Eli” Hoberg**.

Before Sable Harbor, Hoberg works around forestry communications: logging crews, wildland-fire crews, and other workers operating in dense timber and mountainous terrain. He becomes frustrated by organizations spending heavily on radio systems that perform poorly in the actual terrain where crews depend on them. His objection is not that the radios are universally bad; it is that vendors and buyers repeatedly treat the radio as the whole communications system while ignoring terrain, relay placement, propagation, redundancy, and field architecture.

Hoberg begins designing improvised relay/repeater networks and creative communications architectures that make existing equipment work more reliably in forests and mountain ranges. He eventually forms a small specialist company called **Quality Forest Communications**. Its practical reputation is making other people's radios work where ordinary deployments do not.

That background is the direct precursor to his Klein role in underground RF and communications. His experimental RF mapping rig becomes **Theseus**, followed by Theseus II and III as every component is eventually replaced.

sections.heading: WIL-010 — Sar-e-Sang incident detail
sections.text:
**State:** LOCKED event expansion; no criminal or espionage finding

Two Klein personnel travel to Central Asia in 2022 under a loosely authorized industrial-observation and research premise. Their work expands into an approximately three-week unsanctioned journey involving Sar-e-Sang and other mining areas in Badakhshan, Afghanistan.

The access chain is deliberately difficult to reconstruct afterward. A regional minerals contact introduces an intermediary whose institutional affiliations are unclear. The travelers are discouraged from using company branding in some settings, movement is increasingly arranged by people whose names and affiliations are not consistently supplied, and ordinary commercial travel controls break down. Cash is used for transport, access, lodging, guides, and local facilitation. Some receipts are incomplete, some counterparties cannot later be identified to Sable Harbor's satisfaction, and some costs appear to have been paid or subsidized by third parties without a clean explanation.

As the trip progresses, questions directed at the travelers move beyond ordinary mining curiosity. They are asked what Sable Harbor's systems can infer from conflicting records, whether Foundry can identify undeclared physical activity through paperwork discrepancies, and what the company can see across industrial supply chains. At least one traveler records the substance of those questions because they feel out of place in the stated context.

Communications become intermittent and the travelers experience a material period during which Sable Harbor cannot reliably account for their location or itinerary. This is not canonized as a kidnapping or detention. The problem is that the company cannot reconstruct the period with enough confidence to rule out more concerning explanations. After return, leadership also finds route changes, unexplained or poorly supported expense-chain activity, and contextual details that neither traveler can fully explain.

Sable Harbor does **not** conclude that its personnel committed espionage, knowingly financed a terrorist organization, acted as intelligence officers, or knowingly entered an unlawful arrangement. Nor does it conclude that a foreign intelligence or security service targeted the company. The enduring problem is epistemic: leadership cannot confidently establish who some intermediaries represented, why certain questions were asked, who subsidized parts of the movement, or whether the travelers were being informally assessed for reasons unrelated to the stated mining purpose.

The concern becomes serious enough that senior leadership and counsel discuss whether the facts warrant voluntary contact with the **FBI regarding a potential counterintelligence exposure**. That discussion is real and documented internally; it is not treated as melodrama or as proof that a counterintelligence event occurred. The historical record does not assert a criminal referral, investigation, or intelligence finding. The uncertainty itself is consequential.

The incident is therefore both governance failure and institutional near miss. It is a major reason Klein cannot continue in its existing form and directly informs Willow's later bright lines: no freelance diplomacy, no unsanctioned field access, no untraceable cash arrangements, no representations outside delegated authority, and no production deployment without an operating owner and qualification gate.

Its physical archaeology does survive. Old Klein labels, stickers, stencils, prototype names, equipment markings, and at least one historical sign remain visible around Willow where the original object is still in use or deliberately preserved. Retired prototypes and artifacts may be displayed in the yard collection known as **the Museum**. sections.heading: The Fort — Willow's Pittsburgh compound
sections.text:
**State:** LOCKED site concept; exact parcel/address remains implementation detail

Willow's Pittsburgh-area physical center is a roughly **10–20 acre** industrial compound informally and then routinely called **the Fort**. The Fort is a working industrial research site, not a landscaped corporate campus.

The site has three principal structures:

1. **The Big Shed** — Willow's main research building and laboratory. Most experimental work, instrumentation, prototyping, integration, bench work, and hands-on research occurs here. It is explicitly not the primary administrative building and not bulk storage.
2. **The Small Shed** — administrative offices plus a small attached lodging component, effectively a modest internal mini-hotel for temporary stays by visiting staff, collaborators, field personnel, or employees whose work requires them to remain at the Fort for short periods. It is not permanent employee housing.
3. **The White Shed** — controlled intake, secure storage, utility, mechanical, staging, and quarantine space for unusual equipment, samples, field gear, or material that should not move directly onto the Big Shed research floor.

The remaining grounds are intentionally spare: controlled perimeter and gate, gravel circulation, hardstand, outdoor staging, utility/service areas, and practical non-sensitive storage. The working yards and accumulated outdoor collection are collectively known as **the Museum**. The name is affectionate and literal enough to persist: obsolete rigs, retired prototypes, industrial fragments, and odd pieces of equipment can remain because they preserve useful physical history, not because Willow is operating a public museum.

The Fort's naming follows Willow culture: useful, slightly irreverent labels become durable because everyone knows what they mean.

sections.heading: Locked geography, provider selections, and operating model
sections.text:
1. **Primary transitional runtime:** **Switch TAHOE RENO — The Citadel Campus, Nevada** is the selected colocation provider/site for Sable Harbor's Reno primary transitional estate. Sable Harbor-owned compute, storage, network, and key-management equipment will operate in a dedicated controlled Switch environment. This is an owner-approved provider selection and procurement target; it does **not** assert that a contract has been executed, capacity has been reserved, equipment has been installed, or provider controls have been accepted as operating evidence.
2. **Independent recovery runtime:** **IDACORE Boise, 2653 S Victory View Way, Boise, Idaho 83709** is the selected colocation provider/site for the independent recovery estate. Recovery must preserve administrative independence from Reno, independent carrier paths, independent recovery credentials, and recovery keys that do not depend exclusively on Reno. Provider selection does **not** assert executed contract, installed equipment, completed replication, or tested recovery.
3. **Provider-independence rule:** Boise recovery is intentionally operated by a provider other than Switch. No Switch inter-campus service may become the sole recovery path. Carrier and last-mile diversity must be evidenced before recovery acceptance.
4. **Commercial diligence remains an implementation gate, not a provider-selection question.** Procurement must negotiate and document capacity, price, term, expansion rights, audit reports, complementary user-entity controls, subservice organizations, incident obligations, insurance, remote hands, access, cross-connects, exit rights, and the SLA/control requirements in this PR. A material failure to meet mandatory requirements returns the exception to the owner rather than silently substituting another provider.
5. **Owned primary end state:** SABLE HARBOR Northern Nevada Data Center, Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center planning district, Storey County, Nevada, planning pin **39.5450, -119.4550**. This is a fictional Sable Harbor facility in real geography; it is not a claim concerning a real parcel or real-world ownership.
6. **Owned-site acquisition date in the Sable Harbor planning universe:** **2026-09-04**. The acquired planning parcel is **7.5 acres** with planning consideration **$3.0 million**. No real APN is assigned.
7. **Status as of 2026-09-11:** LAND ACQUIRED / PRECONSTRUCTION. Survey/geotechnical/utility/fiber/design/permitting work is authorized and in progress. **No vertical construction, completed shell, commissioned electrical plant, occupied data hall, or operating owned data center may be depicted.**
8. **Initial Switch Reno design:** 75–100 kW usable IT capacity, contractual/physical expansion rights to at least 200–250 kW, liquid-cooling/high-density capability, dual A/B power, and two physically diverse carrier paths. Exact contracted capacity and commercial terms remain implementation evidence until executed.
9. **Initial IDACORE Boise recovery design:** recovery capacity is sized from accepted RTO/RPO and protected-service priorities rather than assumed to be a full production mirror. Current procurement must preserve at least the repository's independent-recovery planning envelope and require dual power-path design, independent connectivity, customer-controlled equipment/keys, and documented recovery expansion rights. Exact contracted kW/racks remain implementation evidence.
10. **Owned-site design:** 10,000–15,000 sq ft initial hardened shell; 250–500 kW initial modular critical plant; practical 1 MW utility/service pathway; preserve a 2 MW expansion pathway where engineering supports it. Installed capacity must not be confused with ultimate site capability.
11. **Migration trigger:** owned critical-plant commitment is gated by measured demand and committed pipeline. Planning trigger is sustained colocated demand approaching 100–150 kW plus credible three-year demand of 200–250 kW. Migration requires completed commissioning, recovery proof, security acceptance, and Finance authorization.
12. **Long-run topology:** owned Northern Nevada primary + IDACORE Boise recovery + separately protected immutable/offline copies. Switch Reno remains available for transition, burst, recovery support, and capacity shocks after primary migration subject to later economics and control acceptance.

sections.heading: The Fort
sections.text:
The [accepted Willow closeout](../../docs/canon/WILLOW_KLEIN_CLOSEOUT_2026-09-06.md) establishes the three named sheds and outdoor Museum.

The Big Shed is a 60 × 30 m single-level research building with varied fabrication, test, instrumentation, RF and integration workspaces. Its 20-person day allocation includes movement between benches, write-up desks and experiment debriefing. The Small Shed places reception and administration at the southern visitor edge. Its 36 × 24 m footprint carries administration below and six temporary guest rooms above. The lodging is a modest visiting-staff component; it is neither permanent housing nor an extra resident workforce. The White Shed's 36 × 24 m single floor segregates intake, quarantine, secure storage and field-gear staging. Equipment reaches the research floor only after controlled release.

The Museum is an outdoor working collection, preserving `SH-FAC-FORT-MUSEUM`. It creates no fourth building. Hardstand supports active staging independently of the collection. The service yard and utilities sit along the controlled eastern route; visitors arrive in the south. A pedestrian route connects administration to research without crossing the receiving apron. A perimeter route reserves emergency/service access; turning, pavement and fire appliance requirements remain engineering dependencies. Stormwater buffers and a separately gated reserve occupy the northern boundary.

The day scenario places 20 people in Big, eight in Small's administration and four in White: 24 conditional workers plus eight visitors. A separate night scenario places six visitors in Small's lodging and zero in the other floors. These scenarios must not be added. Twenty assigned desks, six touchdown places, 38 meeting places, 34 technical work positions and six beds are activity capacities, not a population total. The 24-worker reference comes from the population bridge's conditional Willow assumption, not a September 2026 staffing claim. Thirty parking spaces and 12 bicycle spaces support the design scenario with explicit, unverified mode-share assumptions.

sections.heading: Bedford
sections.text:
The [Cradle closeout](../../docs/canon/CRADLE_CLOSEOUT_2026-09-06.md) places Bedford in Fairmont on a fictional 15–20 acre redeveloped industrial brownfield. It supersedes Belle/Kanawha as Bedford's intended geography. Bedford remains separate from the Demotte host installation and Kelly Gang Mining's Stream 17 host. No host treatment assets, mine liabilities or host employees move into this site model.

Four proposed structures separate analytical/process development; field-unit assembly and refurbishment; intermediate upgrading/blending; and material receipt/outbound logistics. The assembly/refurbishment hall is 48 × 30 m; the other structures are 36 × 24 m. All have one modelled level. Their functions follow accepted canon while their building identities and geometry are explicit implementation assumptions. No new installed chemical process, rail siding, river berth or commercial individual-REE separation operation is created.

Incoming lots remain held and traceable before transfer to upgrading. Released product has separate dispatch staging. Analytical samples move under custody; routine visitors cannot pass through the material yard. Returned or fouled deployment units go to isolated inspection before clean assembly. External delivery access approaches from the east; staff and visitors use the southern edge. Utilities and containment have a reserved zone rather than invented treatment plant equipment. Brownfield, flood, contamination and utility evidence remain required before a real parcel could be selected.

The simultaneous floor allocations are 12 analytical, six assembly, six upgrading and four materials: 18 conditional workers plus ten visitors. Rotation between field deployment and Bedford is not a second workforce. Ten assigned desks, eight meeting places, eight training places and 48 technical positions serve alternative activities; they do not increase the 28-person peak. Twenty-six parking and ten bicycle spaces are planning allowances.

sections.text:

The warehouse gross areas come from accepted operations: Taylor **210,000 square feet / 19,509.6384 m²**, Rawlins **75,000 square feet / 6,967.728 m²**. Their rectangular footprint proportions and handling/support bands are assumptions. Pallet slots remain **11,000 / 4,000** reserved capacity; no new rack, stacking height, throughput, fire loading or installed equipment is inferred. Storage, receiving/quarantine, dispatch, staff support and protected service reservations replace an office-grid treatment.

The twelve facility allocations total **137 FTE = 131 ARU/BS&T + 6 Red Wash receiving**. Those six are a subset of the **128 Red Wash site employees**, not additional employees. Pale Sun's **12 platform employees** remain separate. Therefore neither the last row nor its receiving subset may be added to the facility table as though every row were an independent population. Assigned workforce includes drivers, crews, field and outdoor activity; it does not equal indoor attendance or desks.

Indoor planning peaks are Taylor shop 10, dispatch/crew house 20, Taylor warehouse 8, trucking building 8, Rawlins warehouse 4 and ARU office 14. These **64 hypothetical indoor places** are not a simultaneous enterprise census, hiring authority or shift schedule. Room seats and activity capacities may serve the same people in different activities. The Red Wash stress-test scenario separately considers 48 site workers plus four visitors/contractors; it does not establish actual attendance, installed capacity or statutory egress. Future 2031/2036 positions remain unresolved, with no assumed growth approved.

Every site points to its original georeferenced polygon and original geometry/precision/date fields. Local metric diagram frames reuse source acreage/aspect solely to size an illustrative working envelope; they have no survey transform. Proposed building placements do not replace original geometry or establish rail/road crossing permission. The Red Wash overall 1,000 × 800 m envelope remains a **preliminary engineering proposal**, not owned land or historical disturbance. Its accepted operating anchor remains −108.18, 42.22. The rejected mine rail spur is excluded.

The source preserves references to all **20 facility tracks, 11 route segments and 26 network structures**. The latter comprise bridges, culverts and external highway overbridges and receive context plus their existing engineering record, with a justified floor-plan exemption. Route structures are not assigned arbitrarily to an adjacent building. Existing tracks must be rendered from their accepted geographic geometry; local functional zones are not track alignments. The Taylor shop must be reconciled to the original shop track before engineering acceptance. Heavy locomotive overhaul remains outsourced.

The parent facility generator renders these records using the campus schema with `layout_style: industrial`, preventing automatic office corridor/core overlays. Each source building has its own rooms, gross/net/support areas, explicit perimeter egress concept and floor peak. `map_prefix` uses the existing `SH-MAP-ARU` / `SH-MAP-RWM` families with successor allocations from 020 onward. The shared manifest and atlas own output paths and navigation; this source creates no competing geographic portal.

All building dimensions other than the stated warehouse areas, room use subdivisions, clear heights, structural spans, access reservations, egress assumptions and interior capacities are planning assumptions. Source opening dates describe the established synthetic facilities; they are not dates of the illustrated fitout, ownership transfer or construction completion. Detailed field/as-built evidence, fire engineering, accessibility, structural/loading checks, utility/containment design and operator-approved access are the next actions for technical layers explicitly left unresolved.

sections.heading: Intended structure and real eligibility rules
sections.text:
The legal transaction is SHIH's purchase of 100% of ARU stock on January 7, 2026. A §338(h)(10) election generally treats an eligible target as making a deemed asset sale and liquidation for federal tax purposes. A qualified stock purchase requires at least 80% of voting power and value acquired by a corporation within the prescribed twelve-month period. The election is joint; every S target shareholder must participate. Form 8023 ordinarily is due on the fifteenth day of the ninth month after acquisition, yielding October 15, 2026 here. [IRS Form 8023 instructions, October 2023 revision](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i8023).

S eligibility requires a domestic eligible corporation, allowable shareholders, no more than 100 shareholders and one stock class. Corporate shareholders and nonresident alien shareholders are ineligible. [IRS S corporation requirements](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/s-corporations).

sections.heading: Synthetic facts chosen to satisfy that structure
sections.text:
| Fact | Case implementation and evidence boundary |
|---|---|
| Purchasing corporation | SHIH is a Delaware C corporation and purchases every ARU share; no rollover or disqualified partial purchase is modeled |
| Target | ARU is a Wyoming domestic corporation with a valid pre-close S election, represented uninterrupted through the relevant pre-close period |
| Sellers | Fred Tolman 60%, Adele Tolman 20%, Nora Ashcombe 10%, Seth Kettering 10%; four U.S.-citizen natural persons, no trusts/entities or nonresident holders |
| Stock rights | One identical economic common class; no side distributions creating preferred rights; management service payments separately documented |
| Election cooperation | Buyer and all four sellers supply the intended joint election signature packet at close |
| Submission state | March 2 internal filing-ready review exists; this package does not establish actual IRS filing or acceptance. Controller's deadline remains tracked |
| Post-close ARU | Corporate buyer makes the prior S shareholder conditions unavailable; the case continues ARU as a wholly owned C corporate subsidiary |

These are synthetic eligibility facts, not authentic historical election certificates. No actual tax ID, government stamp, letter of acceptance or filing confirmation is fabricated. “Filing-ready” is not silently promoted to “filed.” If the election is not timely and validly made, the deemed-sale basis case is unavailable and the alternative tax-basis scenario must be used; the share purchase itself does not disappear.

sections.heading: BS&T subsidiary treatment
sections.text:
ARU's wholly owned domestic railroad is modeled as a valid QSub from January 1, 2008 until the acquisition-related termination. IRS explains that a valid QSub election makes the subsidiary's assets, liabilities and tax items those of the S parent for federal tax purposes; it does not require an actual corporate dissolution. QSub eligibility requires complete ownership by an eligible S parent. [IRS Form 8869 instructions, December 2020 revision](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i8869).

The case therefore includes the railroad's assets and liabilities in the old-ARU deemed-sale model while preserving BS&T's legal company, regulatory duties, workforce and separate operating books. This is an application of the cited QSub treatment to the explicitly assumed case facts, not a separate BS&T §338 election. The post-close corporate ownership/tax model must reflect termination of QSub status and continuity of the legal railroad. No deduction or asset-basis amount is established merely by calling a subsidiary a QSub.

sections.heading: Book purchase accounting and tax allocation
sections.text:
The book acquisition model measures the acquired net assets, retained liabilities, fees and goodwill independently of legal stock form. It is a synthetic PPA, not an audited appraisal. The tax allocation must distinguish purchase consideration, liabilities included under the tax model, asset-class basis, nondeductible transaction costs, financing costs and temporary differences. Equal book/tax starting values are a model assumption only where explicitly supported; accrued environmental/claim costs and later deductions cannot be ignored to force deferred tax to zero.

The January 1–6 stub in the financial source is an **economic closing bridge**. It is not an assertion that old-target federal tax reporting ends January 6. The tax analysis separately considers the January 7 acquisition-date deemed sale and the prescribed old/new-target timing; it does not move the locked legal close or backdate the buyer's economic control.

The controller maintains one reconciliation from the agreed allocation to the book PPA, tax-basis schedule and modeled deferred taxes. Seller-period obligations, tax-return cooperation, allocation consistency and any later true-up remain separately identified. The participant can test the validity and consequences of those assumptions without being told that a regulator approved them.

The derived financial case recognizes a conditional $587,500 deferred-tax asset for the $1.75M environmental accrual and $0.60M claim accrual at a modeled combined 25% rate. It assumes eventual recovery through additional deductible acquired-asset basis, not an automatic immediate expense deduction when either reserve is paid. Both the tax rate and full realizability are explicit case assumptions. Identifiable net assets become $33,237,500 and book goodwill $14,762,500 against $48M stock consideration. No reserve settlement or reserve deferred-tax reversal is assumed in 2026. Debt issuance costs are presented against debt, separately from expensed transaction fees. The generated finance reconciliation controls subsequent changes to these model assumptions.

The separate opening tax allocation is $48M stock basis plus $20M recognized assumed liabilities, producing $68M modeled adjusted grossed-up basis. Those liabilities comprise $3M payables, $1M operating accruals, $13.5M term/revolver debt and $2.5M leases. Other acquired tax asset bases total $55M: cash $2M, receivables $6M, inventory $1.8M, prepaids $0.7M, owned PPE $42M and conditionally tax-owned leased property $2.5M. Residual **tax goodwill is $13M**, independently calculated from the book PPA. Net receivable tax basis, tax ownership of leased assets and zero additional buyer-cost allocation are disclosed conditional classifications; parent transaction-cost tax treatment is outside the forecast.

The $2.35M environmental/claim reserves are excluded from that opening tax purchase-price measure pending economic performance. General assumed-liability principles distinguish acquisition from later recognition in purchaser basis; a later settlement can require redetermined acquisition basis and amortization rather than an immediate deduction. The IRS discussion supporting that distinction appears in [Treasury Decision 9158, Bulletin 2004-42](https://www.irs.gov/irb/2004-42_IRB) and [Treasury Decision 9358, Bulletin 2007-41](https://www.irs.gov/irb/2007-41_IRB). Their nuclear-decommissioning-specific provisions are not applied to this ordinary industrial acquisition. The case uses the general timing principle only; its actual liability classifications remain assumptions.

Opening book goodwill exceeds tax goodwill by $1,762,500. The model separately identifies that initial component and recognizes no opening goodwill deferred-tax liability under a conditional initial-recognition accounting judgment. This is not an independently verified accounting opinion. Subsequent tax amortization creates a separately measured deferred-tax liability; the initial difference is not silently amortized as though it were tax basis.

Acquired qualifying goodwill is generally a §197 intangible amortized for federal tax over 180 months beginning with the acquisition month. That tax rule is separate from the model's nonamortizing book goodwill. [IRS Form 4562 instructions](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i4562), [IRS intangible-assets guidance](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/intangibles).

The elected-case tax rollforward therefore separately identifies its assumed tax-goodwill basis, monthly deduction and resulting book/tax difference. The finance model carries the resulting deferred-tax liability instead of asserting perpetual book/tax equality. Annual current-tax measurement uses cumulative taxable income, while scheduled cash payments and any tax payable or overpayment remain separate balances. A winter book loss is not erased by independently taxing each later profitable month. These synthetic measurement conventions remain conditional on the election, actual allocation and deduction eligibility; this memorandum does not certify a filed return.
